rationale:
Evidence: no race telemetry exists yet, so every choice rests on the contract and the round-1 critique. I accepted most of the critique and rejected none outright.

Accepted and changed:
1) Speed. A 4-5 m course in under 3 s needs about 1.5-1.67 m/s average, so base_speed 1.5 is at the minimum with no margin. Real speed will fall below the PWM-based estimate from rolling resistance, slip, battery sag and slowing on tight bends. I raised base_speed to 1.8 (PWM about 90 percent). This is a compromise: a completion failure costs 500 points, so the margin matters more than the time bonus, but 1.8 is high enough to make the 3 s limit achievable. Expected failure mode: if completion_time is above about 2.9 s with completion 1, raise base_speed; if the robot leaves the track on the slalom, lower it.
2) Look-ahead. Sensors move from y 0.03 to y 0.06 m, adding about 30 ms of lead at 1.8 m/s. This is the critique's main lever for bends.
3) Steady offset. ki goes from 0 to 0.3. The motor mismatch causes a constant bias under P+D control, and the integral is already clamped to +/-2, so the integral term is capped at about 0.6 turn (about 210 PWM). This is limited enough to avoid windup.
4) Coverage. Sensor footprint goes from 12 mm to 16 mm. At the 20 mm pitch this removes the 8 mm gaps, so the tape is always read by at least one sensor. The cost is a slightly less sharp response.

Kept unchanged: sensor x positions and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] (linear, antisymmetric, so the sign convention holds), kp 2.5, kd 0.2, line_loss last_direction, wheel_track, wheel_radius and mass. kd 0.2 is kept: with 16 mm footprints the signal is smoother, so derivative noise should be lower than my estimate of about 200 PWM counts from the critique; the race will show this in steering_oscillation.

Rejected or corrected: the critique's point about body_width is correct arithmetic, but I keep body_width 0.12 because it is in range and has no effect on dynamics. I did not change it to chase an off-track allowance that does not exist at this value. Signal nonlinearity is acknowledged; I keep kp at 2.5 because it is a moderate value that is hard to tune without data.

Delta from draft: base_speed 1.5 to 1.8, sensor y 0.03 to 0.06, sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, ki 0 to 0.3. Expected result: completion 1 with completion_time about 2.6-2.9 s, rms_error under about 0.03 m, few line-loss events. If oscillation appears at this speed, the next revision should lower kp before changing base_speed.
